record.context_brief: Generating series for rational points of arithmetic varieties
record.original_question: Let (V,L) be a projective manifold over a number field k together with a metrized ample sheaf, so that one has a height function h_L: V(k) → R and an associated height zeta function Z(V,L;s)=Σ_{x∈V(k)} h_L(x)^(-s). For varieties V that are not toric, the source says that this zeta function does not seem to have satisfactory analytic properties, unlike classical Hasse-Weil-Serre L-functions. Can one find a class of generating series that counts the rational points V(k) in a mathematically useful way and has good analytic behavior?

evidence.quote: Let (V,L) be a projective manifold over a number field k endowed with a metrized ample sheaf allowing one to construct the height function h_L : V(k) → R. The naive problem of finding asymptotics for the number of k-points of bounded height has the refined version: to understand the analytic properties of the height zeta-function Z(V,L;s) = Σ_{x∈V(k)} h_L(x)^-s.
Unfortunately, it seems that if V is not homogeneous or something like that, Z(V,L;s) does not have good analytic properties, unlike the more traditional Hasse-Weil-Serre ..., L-functions.
The problem I want to draw attention to is: Find a class of good generating series counting V(k).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a number field and let $V$ be a smooth projective variety over $k$. Let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $V$ equipped with an adelic metric, giving rise to a height function $h_L : V(k) \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}$. The associated height zeta function is the Dirichlet-type series
$$Z(V,L;s) \;=\; \sum_{x \in V(k)} h_L(x)^{-s},$$
which converges in some right half-plane whenever $V(k)$ is not too dense. For toric varieties and certain homogeneous spaces, $Z(V,L;s)$ is known to admit a meromorphic continuation with controlled poles, encoding precise asymptotics for the number of rational points of bounded height. However, for general (non-homogeneous) projective varieties $V$, the height zeta function $Z(V,L;s)$ is not expected to have good analytic properties (e.g. meromorphic continuation, functional equation, or a controlled set of poles) comparable to those of classical Hasse–Weil–Serre $L$-functions.

Problem: Construct a class of generating series associated with the pair $(V,L)$ over $k$, different from the naive height zeta function $Z(V,L;s)$, with the following properties:
(a) the series genuinely counts (or weights) the rational points $V(k)$, in a way that recovers meaningful arithmetic information such as asymptotics for points of bounded height;
(b) the series possesses good analytic behavior, including meromorphic continuation to a large region of $\mathbb{C}$, a precise description of its poles, and ideally a functional equation, holding for a class of varieties $V$ broader than toric or homogeneous ones.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a programmatic open question in the style of Manin's program on rational points. Refined conjectures (Batyrev–Manin, Peyre, Batyrev–Tschinkel) describe expected leading asymptotics, and height zeta functions have been analyzed for toric varieties, equivariant compactifications of algebraic groups, and certain fibrations. However, no general satisfactory class of "good" generating series for arbitrary non-homogeneous projective varieties is known, and the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Manin's conjecture (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Manin's conjecture predicts asymptotics for rational points of bounded height; proven only in special cases (toric, equivariant compactifications, etc.).
status_evidence.claim: General analytic theory of height zeta functions for arbitrary varieties remains open.

status_evidence.title: Batyrev–Tschinkel, Tamagawa numbers and rational points
status_evidence.snippet: Height zeta functions are studied for equivariant compactifications; general non-homogeneous case lacks analogous results.
status_evidence.claim: Good analytic behavior is established only for restricted classes.
